hints: Use the cuboid directions: $\mathbf i$ is along $OA$, $\mathbf j$ along $OD$, and $\mathbf k$ along $OC$.
Locate $E$ and $F$ from the edge lengths, then average their position vectors because $M$ is their midpoint.
Express the resulting position vector in $\mathbf i,\mathbf j,\mathbf k$ components.
walkthrough:
Set up the coordinates of the cuboid vertices based on the given dimensions $OA = 3$ (along $\mathbf{i}$), $OD = 2$ (along $\mathbf{j}$), and $OC = 2$ (along $\mathbf{k}$):
$$E = (3, 2, 0) \quad \text{and} \quad F = (3, 2, 2)$$

hints: Form the two vectors from the vertex of the required angle: $\overrightarrow{AM}=2\mathbf j+\mathbf k$ and $\overrightarrow{AP}=-2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+2\mathbf k$.
Calculate the dot product and both magnitudes, then apply inverse cosine in the desired angular unit.
A general point $Q$ on the line through $O$ and $M$ has position vector $\mu(3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)$.
Form $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mu(3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)-(\mathbf i+\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)$.
At the perpendicular foot, impose $\overrightarrow{PQ}\cdot(3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)=0$ and solve for $\mu$.
Substitute this value into $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and take its magnitude, leaving the length exact.
walkthrough:
Write the vector equation of the line passing through $O$ and $M$ with direction vector $\mathbf{d} = 3\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \mu(3\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})$$

Let $Q$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $P(1, 1, 2)$ on the line $OM$:
$$\vec{OQ} = 3\mu\mathbf{i} + 2\mu\mathbf{j} + \mu\mathbf{k}$$

Calculate the exact length of the perpendicular $|\vec{PQ}|$:
$$|\vec{PQ}| = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 0^2 + \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{9}{4}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{10}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{2}$$
